title: Multitenant Spotlight Auditor: Design and Operator Runbook
author: Jordan Kim
body:
> **Archived 2026-02-15:** this page is superseded by "Multitenant Spotlight Auditor and Remediation Playbook" and is kept for reference only.

Summary
-------
The Multitenant Spotlight Auditor (MSA) is a service plus operator toolkit that finds, scores, and helps fix tenant-level unfairness on the inference platform. It pulls together scheduler events, KV/prefix cache telemetry, token-cost attribution, and tail-latency traces, and outputs a ranked list of tenants and workloads that need an operator or an automated mitigation.

Goals
-----
- Spot tenants whose behavior has outsized resource impact (latency spikes, cache thrashing, batching stalls, token leakage).
- Give operators auditable comparisons and a repeatable remediation runbook.
- Support safe automated mitigations with escalation to a human.
- Surface fairness and cost impact to platform ops and product via dashboards and alerts.

Out of scope
------------
- Billing disputes and adjustments (Finance owns these).
- Rate-limiting policy wording shown to tenants (API gateway owns this).

When to use MSA
---------------
- Unexplained regional latency degradation that coincides with a change in tenant mix.
- Token-cost variance that workload shape does not explain.
- Capacity planning experiments that need to validate fairness models.

Architecture (high level)
-------------------------
1) Ingest: scheduled jobs and streaming collectors joining traces, cost attribution, scheduler events, and prefix-KV cache telemetry.
2) Scoring Engine: batch and streaming jobs that compute per-tenant impact scores (latency externality, cache churn index, token-leak factor).
3) Operator UI & Automation: ranked incident dashboard, suggested remediations, and automation routines (soft-throttle, tenant-priority-reshuffle, canary requeue).

Data flow (text):
- Traces, token-cost attribution, and scheduler events feed the collectors
- Collectors -> enrichment (join on request_id / prefix_key) -> scoring engine -> audit DB
- Operator UI reads the audit DB and calls platform APIs to run playbook actions

Key signals
-----------
- tenant_id, window_start, window_end
- requests_per_minute, p99_latency_ms, mean_queue_depth
- cache_prefix_evictions, kv_cache_hit_rate (0..1)
- token_burn_adjusted -- tokens charged after prefix caching adjustments
- externality_score (0..100) -- composite from the scoring engine

Scoring heuristics
------------------
- latency_externality = max(0, p99 - baseline_p99) * weight_latency
- cache_churn_index = normalized(cache_prefix_evictions) * weight_cache
- token_leak_factor = log(1 + token_burn_adjusted / tenant_avg) * weight_token
- externality_score = scaled_sum of the three components

Baselines are computed per region and per hardware class so mixed fleets do not generate false positives.

Alerting rules (proposed)
-------------------------
- Alert: tenant-spotlight-high-externality
  - Trigger: externality_score >= 70 for 15m AND tenant not in "trusted-tier" list
  - Severity: P2
  - Runbook: MSA triage runbook below
- Alert: repeated-cache-thrashing
  - Trigger: cache_prefix_evictions > 10k in 5m AND kv_cache_hit_rate < 0.35
  - Severity: P3

Dashboard panels (proposed)
---------------------------
- Ranked table: tenant, region, externality_score, p99, token_burn_adjusted, recommended_action
- Time series: top-10 tenants p99 against region baseline
- Heatmap: cache evictions per prefix_key across nodes
- Cost view: token_burn attribution stacked by tenant and model

Runbook: Triage & Remediation
-----------------------------
1) Acknowledge the alert and open the tenant's MSA entry.
2) From the ranked table, open the tenant timeline and collect p99, p50, queue depth, cache eviction trend, and served model version.
3) Review recent scheduler placement changes for noisy collocated tenants.
4) High cache_churn_index:
   a) Pin the tenant to a dedicated prefix cache shard if one is free.
   b) For quick relief, raise the soft TTL on small prefixes:

   ```
   rcd platform cache update-ttl --prefix tenant-abc --ttl 120s --reason "MSA mitigation: reduce evictions"
   ```

5) High token_leak_factor:
   a) Run a prompt-set audit for patterns that defeat caching (Appendix Query A).
   b) Suggest quantization or batching changes and loop in solutions engineering.

6) Latency externality dominant with no config fix:
   a) Soft-throttle the tenant (10-20% throughput reduction) by lowering its priority weight:

   ```
   rcd scheduler set-priority --tenant tenant-abc --weight 0.8 --duration 30m --reason "MSA temporary fairness throttle"
   ```

7) Watch externality_score for 2 windows (15m each) after mitigation. If it has not dropped by 50%, escalate in the Platform Escalation channel and follow the emergency-model-swap runbook.

Automation guardrails
---------------------
- One on-call operator must approve automation actions, except low-impact ones (ttl tweak <= 120s, soft-priority <= 5%) which may run automatically.
- Automation never changes tenant billing or customer-visible SLA text.
- Every automated action writes an audit record: actor, reason, pre- and post-metrics snapshot.
- Each automated change declares a rollback window (default 45m) and auto-reverts if externality_score gets worse.

Rollout plan
------------
1) Canary (2 weeks): passive scoring in 10% of regions, no automation, read-only alerts.
2) Operator trial (4 weeks): manual action buttons enabled, gather feedback, tune weights.
3) Controlled automation (6 weeks): low-impact automated actions behind 1-operator approval.
4) Full rollout: automation policy with standard guardrails and a monthly audit.

Rollout metrics
- False-positive rate of top-20 flagged tenants (target < 10%)
- Operator time-to-remediation (target < 45 minutes after acknowledging)
- Automation rollback rate (target < 5%)

Ownership and dependencies
--------------------------
- Owner: eng-platform/tenant-observability squad (oncall: @tenant-observability)
- Depends on: token cost attribution service (engineering/infra), KV/prefix cache telemetry (eng-serving-runtime), scheduler events stream (eng-platform/scheduler)
- Roadmap: Optimize recommendations integration and a tenant-level notice for support are planned for later in 2026.

Quick templates
---------------
- Template A: Cache evictions -- when cache_prefix_evictions > 5x baseline and kv_cache_hit_rate < 0.4: update-ttl + pin-prefix-shard + notify product owner
- Template B: Latency externality -- when p99 > baseline + 200ms and queue_depth > 3: lower tenant weight by 10% for 30m and monitor

Appendix: Example queries
-------------------------
```sql
SELECT tenant_id,
       SUM(externality_score) AS score,
       MAX(p99_latency_ms) AS p99
FROM msa.tenant_window
WHERE window_start >= now() - interval '1 hour'
GROUP BY tenant_id
ORDER BY score DESC
LIMIT 50;
```

```promql
msa_externality_score{region="us-east-1"} > 70
```

FAQ
---
- Why no automatic throttling by default? -> Human-in-loop protects customer SLAs.
- How are weights tuned? -> Offline sensitivity tests on synthetic workloads, checked against historical incidents.

Contact
-------
- eng-platform/tenant-observability squad (oncall) and the runtime-telemetry team.
- Security-sensitive incidents: follow security-and-compliance/incident-response-security procedures.
